I'm not sure.  La Comodora is probably my favorite character of the bunch, but I have no idea how she plays.  Harpy, Benchmark, and Idealist look fiddly, and fiddly heroes often don't work well in practice.  Akash'Thriya looks extremely fiddly and setup-heavy, and I cannot imagine how she functions from what I've seen--I like the idea a lot but I don't have high hopes.  Conversely, Stuntman doesn't appeal to me on paper, but the playtesters are loving him.

So basically, I'm avoiding getting "excited" about any hero in particular so I don't get disappointed.  I don't want to get my heart set on making Writhe one of my go-to characters and them have him be no better than Expatriette or Mainstay.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Alright, I'm doing this.  The thing I most enjoy about each character, without spoiling things.

Akash'Thriya:  The mechanics of her deck.  It is so different.

Benchmark:  The culmination.  Benchmark has some fantastic synergy, and I love the feeling of when it pays off.  

La Commodora:  the versatility.  She has a lot of fun stuff to do, fitting her to the situation so she's most valuable is what I like from her gameplay.

Dr. Medico:  How to put this. . . The non-healing parts?  (Not spoiling is hard)

The Harpy:  There's this one card in her deck that I love more than any other card, mechanically speaking (well, maybe not more than Zealous Offense).  When Christopher dropped it into the deck it was like a universal moment of true avian harmony, deafening and magical and perfect.

Idealist:  Super Sentai Idealist.  Yes I could use this deck to do things written on the cards (which, don't get me wrong, is fun) or I could build a giant robot.  Not a hard choice for me.

Lifeline:  the big turns where you do all the things.

Luminary:  Easy one, the destroying everything and then laughing maniacally part.

Mainstay:  Screw strategy, it's time to break things.

Stuntman:  Honestly, the card art and flavor text.  The deck is great fun, but the art and flavor is next level.

Writhe:  the swings between feeling vulnerable and invincible.

posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
Phantom5613:

I want all of them…I guess, if I HAVE to pick one… Benchmark, since Power Armor/Robo-Cop?

A little bit more of explination for this comment: I have a few favorite archetypes when it comes to superheroes. Two of these are Archer and Power Armor.

One can say that we've had those archetypes filled out with Parse and Bunker respectivley, and I love playing both of them(Heck, Bunker was the first deck I played, and Parse is my first position go-to for any high-level villains), but they don't really fit the 'classic' idea of either of those archetypes. Which is one of the reasons I love the inclusion of Bowman in 'Sentinels of Earth-Prime'. He's a classic trick archer superhero along the lines of Green Arrow or Hawkeye, someone who has no powers or 'meta-human' abbilities but makes up for it with quick wit and reflexes and incredible aim. Again, I love Parse. But her playstyle just doesn't scratch my 'trick archer' itch.(So much that I've maid my own fan-deck archer inspired from my old 'City of Heroes' days.)

The same can be said for Bunker. Now, I LOVE having him fully set-up and about to blast away at a bunch of minions as he blasts away the main villain with a 15-card charged Omni-Cannon, but still I have that urge to build my own power armor user who flies through the sky and fires energy blasts at minions as he weaves through a volley of missiles, all the while surveying the scene and calculationg the best way for your allies to bust through the enemy's defenses.

Here's to Benchmark possibly making me feel that way that Bunker never could.
